summary: Practise applying IHL references to protection and access decisions. Explore the five-day humanitarian law training and course outline.
lede: International humanitarian law training helps humanitarian protection and operations staff apply core rules to field decisions. Learners practise identifying protected persons, assessing civilian-harm concerns and access constraints, and documenting decisions within operational role boundaries. The foundation-level course also develops skills in using treaty and customary IHL references, handling incident information cautiously, and preparing referral records and protection decision briefs.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who make, document or review protection and access decisions in humanitarian operations. It suits foundation-level learners who need to apply core international rules to practical field situations.
modules: ICRC Customary IHL in Field Decisions
prerequisites: No formal legal background is required. Familiarity with humanitarian programming or field operations is useful but not essential. Coding or programming is not required.
